scope.flow: Campaign creation: gross amount validated against rewardTokenMinAmounts, then fees subtracted to yield stored/distributed net amount

statements.text: The campaign creator supplies a gross amount exactly at the minimum per hour, so the gross amount passes the rewardTokenMinAmounts validation.
Non-zero protocol fees apply to the campaign amount.
The campaign creator submits campaign creation with the minimum valid gross amount.
The contract enforces rewardTokenMinAmounts on the gross amount supplied by the creator.
Protocol fees are computed and subtracted after the minimum check, producing campaignAmountMinusFees.
There is no second validation that the net amount campaignAmountMinusFees still satisfies the minimum per-epoch constraint before it is stored in newCampaign.amount and distributed.
A campaign's stored and distributed net amount per epoch should not fall below the guardian-configured rewardTokenMinAmounts floor.
Campaigns can be created that appear to satisfy the guardian's minimum emission requirement but in practice emit less than rewardTokenMinAmounts per epoch.
Recipients are systematically underpaid relative to the whitelist floor and to what governance/guardian intended to enforce.

The protocol's policy lever of no campaign below X per epoch is weakened: non-zero fees silently push actual emissions below the configured threshold whenever creators choose the minimum valid gross amount.
This constitutes a broken protocol-level guarantee and can lead to underfunded reward programs and incorrect economic assumptions, with no direct theft of funds beyond the configured fee.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the scenario was observed in a real transaction; conditions are conditional (whenever creators choose the minimum valid gross amount).
No explicit actor authorization or permissionless-call statement is given; campaign creator role inferred from description.
Exact fee value and resulting net amount are not quantified in the report.
